title: Legacy UFO program secrecy rooted in the Manhattan Project and the 1954 Atomic Energy Act

tellings.quote: specifically legacy programs starting with the same secrecy mechanisms as the Manhattan project and the 1954 atomic energy agreement birthing a lot of the secrecy behind uh UFO legacy program classification and controls.
SEC. 141. POLICY.—It shall be the policy of the Commission to control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security.

r. The term 'Restricted Data' means all data concerning (1) design, manufacture, or utilization of atomic weapons; (2) the production of special nuclear material; or (3) the use of special nuclear material in the production of energy, but shall not include data declassified or removed from the Restricted Data category pursuant to section 142.

plain: An online researcher who goes by UAPGerb tells Michels that the secret, long-running "legacy" UFO programmes were built on the same secrecy rules as the Manhattan Project, the wartime effort to build the atomic bomb. He says the Atomic Energy Act of 1954 gave birth to much of their classification. He draws on what the whistleblower David Grusch has said, and if he is right, the nuclear secrecy system has been hiding UFO work all along. The act, which Congress passed on 30 August 1954, says the Atomic Energy Commission should "control the dissemination and declassification of Restricted Data in such a manner as to assure the common defense and security". It defines Restricted Data as information on atomic weapons and nuclear material, and it does not mention unidentified objects or any programme for them.

discussion.by: Atomic Energy Act of 1954 (Public Law 703, 83rd Congress, 68 Stat. 919)
discussion.text: The teller does not say which part of the 1954 act he means; if it is its secrecy rules, the act puts the control of Restricted Data (data on atomic weapons and on special nuclear material) with the Atomic Energy Commission "to assure the common defense and security". It does not mention unidentified objects or any program for them.
